title: Initial scan-loop behavior
statement: Fix a scan task, natural numbers $n,iv,tv,B$, bit strings $w,E$, an oracle $o$, and a bit string $rest$. Let $X(n,w)=\langle 1^n,w\rangle$, using the self-delimiting pair encoding. Suppose the oracle answers each query $X(n,\operatorname{bits}(p))$ with the $p$th bit of $E$, defaulting to false; the target condition holds, meaning that for the edge task the two decoded words of $X(n,w)$ are $\operatorname{bits}(iv)$ and $\operatorname{bits}(tv)$, and for either other task its plain decoded word is $\operatorname{bits}(tv)$; and $|E|\le B$. Suppose also that $E=1^n 0::rest$, and that whenever $n\le tv$, the scan machine halts from label $gA$ with registers $(n+1,n,0)$, respecting the bound $B$ on every register throughout, and returns the bit $ans$. Then for every $j\le n$ with $j\le tv$, the machine halts from label $nA$ with registers $(j,j,0)$, respecting the same register bound, and returns $nAns$ if $tv<n$, and otherwise returns $ans$.
hypotheses_covered: A scan task, $n,iv,tv,B$, bit strings $w,E,rest$, and oracle $o$
Oracle queries on $X(n,\operatorname{bits}(p))$ return the corresponding bit of $E$, defaulting to false
The target decoded-word condition for the selected task
If $n\le tv$, the specified run from label $gA$ halts with answer $ans$ and all registers bounded by $B$
Conclusion ranges over $j\le n$ and $j\le tv$
